chunks.l2:
[tal-a23-v01] Then the rite of consecration is told by the supreme Lord.

[tal-a23-v10] Kuṇḍa and gola are wicked; this is said in the Devyākhyayāmala; and one reborn with another gender is again established in Śaiva.

[tal-a23-v02] This rite, spoken in putraka initiation, is for guru and sadhaka too; it is entitled and endowed with knowledge of bhogya-tattva, in due order.

[tal-a23-v03] Having known him to be a well-practiced knower, a being desiring to become a future one, and fit, the guru should confer his own authority to him.

[tal-a23-v04] Whoever does not know thus is not even consecrated; the teacher is set out by the order of samaya and the rest, as said in the glorious Kāmika.

[tal-a23-v05] He who does not know the sixfold path-union, situated externally and internally, is not a guru who releases, according to the Siddhayogīśvarīmata.

[tal-a23-v06] Even one who lacks all marks, if he possesses knowledge, is regarded as a guru; thus knowledge-primacy is indeed stated in Sri Kacabhargava.

[tal-a23-v07] The guru knows words, sentences, and valid means of knowledge; is solely devoted to Shiva; understands the meaning of all Shiva scriptures; and is compassionate.

[tal-a23-v08] The Supreme Lord himself states the characteristic of the self-born: the non-devotee whose thought is fixed on mere living, though he acts under Īśāna's control, is not (self-born).

[tal-a23-v09] One born from a later self is self-born but not entitled; nor is the mere "sprout of ash" entitled anywhere, nor the son of a vow-keeper, nor likewise the son of bad character.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-:C23 atha śrītantrāloke trayoviṃśatitamamāhnikam athābhiṣekasya vidhiḥ kathyate pārameśvaraḥ yaiṣā putrakadīkṣoktā gurusādhakayorapi / saivādhikāriṇī bhogyatattvayuktimatī kramāt svabhyastajñāninaṃ santaṃ bubhūṣumatha bhāvinam / yogyaṃ jñātvā svādhikāraṃ gurustasmai samarpayet yo naivaṃ veda naivāsāvabhiṣikto@pi daiśikaḥ / samayyādikrameṇeti śrīmatkāmika ucyate yo na vedādhvasandhānaṃ ṣoḍhā bāhyāntarasthitam / sa gururmocayenneti siddhayogīśvarīmate sarvalakṣaṇahīno@pi jñānavān gururiṣyate / jñānaprādhānyamevoktamiti śrīkacabhārgave padavākyapramāṇajñaḥ śivabhaktyekatatparaḥ / samastaśivaśāstrārthaboddhā kāruṇiko guruḥ na svayaṃbhūstasya coktaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ parameśinā / abhakto jīvitadhiyā kurvannīśānadhiṣṭhitaḥ paścātmanā svayaṃbhūṣṇurnādhikārī sa kutracit / bhasmāṅkuro vratisuto duḥśīlātanayastathā kuṇḍo golaśca te duṣṭā uktaṃ devyākhyayāmale / punarbhūścānyaliṅgo yaḥ punaḥ śaive pratiṣṭhitaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a23-v11] In the Śrīpūrvaśāstra no such rule is stated; one who knows the true reality assembly is thus a revealer to the disciple.

[tal-a23-v12] Again, one who knows all principles and the like, and the characteristic in Yogacara, should practice wherever in tantra it is taught, as it is taught.

[tal-a23-v13] Thus indeed, for success, this command is declared; but there, the ritual teacher excludes one-eyed and similar persons.

[tal-a23-v14] Because action is nowhere greater than the completeness of the agent; and in the Devi Yamala scripture there is avoidance of Kanci and similar places.

[tal-a23-v15] Since faults such as anger are seen, how can that be in a well-knowing teacher? But teachers such as Svayambhu and others are to be avoided in the Yamala and similar texts.

[tal-a23-v16] They explained all that by ritual intent; therefore there is the conception of place, family, conduct, and bodily marks.

[tal-a23-v17] Disregarding all else, the guru should make the disciple a guru: having worshipped as before and offered oblation, he causes him to hear the intended matter.

[tal-a23-v18] Then the guru consecrates the disciple with sixty-four; then, once, with that mantra-essence water, by the previously stated rite.

[tal-a23-v19] Then, by abundance and in a well-spread way, he would tell him his own all duty-essence, the supreme secret of the scriptures.

[tal-a23-v20] The disciples you should favor are those impelled by Shiva-Shakti; this was stated in the Jnanottara; and these are Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, and Vaishyas.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-śrīpūrvaśāstre na tveṣa niyamaḥ ko@pi coditaḥ / yathārthatattvasaṃghajñastathā śiṣye prakāśakaḥ yaḥ punaḥ sarvatattvāni vettītyādi ca lakṣaṇam / yogacāre ca yadyatra tantre coditamācaret tathaiva siddhaye seyamājñeti kila varṇitam / yastu karmitayācāryastatra kāṇādivarjanam yataḥ kārakasāmagryātkarmaṇo nādhikaḥ kvacit / devyā yāmalaśāstre ca kāñcyādiparivarjanam taddṛṣṭadoṣātkrodhādeḥ samyakjñātaryasau kutaḥ / guravastu svayaṃbhvādi varjyaṃ yadyāmalādiṣu karmyabhiprāyataḥ sarvaṃ taditi vyācacakṣire / ato deśakulācāradehalakṣaṇakalpanām anādṛtyaiva saṃpūrṇajñānaṃ kuryādgururgurum / prāgvatsaṃpūjya hutvā ca śrāvayitvā cikīrṣitam tato@bhiṣiñcettaṃ śiṣyaṃ catuḥṣaṣṭyā tataḥ sakṛt / tanmantrarasatoyena pūrvoktavidhinā guruḥ vibhavena suvistīrṇaṃ tatastasmai vadetsvakam / sarvaṃ kartavyasāraṃ yacchāstrāṇāṃ paramaṃ rahaḥ anugrāhyāstvayā śiṣyāḥ śivaśaktipracoditāḥ / uktaṃ jñānottare caitadbrāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā viśaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a23-v21] Eunuchs, women, śūdras, and others who desire that are not to be examined in initiation; they should be examined at the time of knowledge.

[tal-a23-v22] The teacher, rooted in knowledge, is declared to conduct the seven-sacrifice: initiation, explanation, compassion, friendship, reflection on scripture, and unity with Shiva.

[tal-a23-v23] In the consecration rite, food-giving and related offerings sustain the seven-sacrifice, and karaṇī, khaṭikā, and related items are given to him.

[tal-a23-v24] All the throng of equipment is to be offered to the wise one; the one consecrated should afterwards honor the teacher with gifts.

[tal-a23-v25] A teacher without knowledge, having handed over his own authority to a ritual worker, should not perform initiation and authority without doing so again by his command.

[tal-a23-v26] Thus he should make him hear; even he should bow and greet. Then from that point on, the former teacher is one who has relinquished authority.

[tal-a23-v27] As he wishes, he may move about in teaching, initiation, and related matters, free from restraint; he is not hindered in acting, because such transmission is like one lamp from another.

[tal-a23-v28] In the Siddhanta tantra it is said that the lineage of non-authority is hindered: falling while acting, and before that, acting itself would be hindered.

[tal-a23-v29] But a teacher who gives instruction according to its meaning is not called contemptuous toward liberation from saṃsāra at the time of the rite.

[tal-a23-v30] A guru endowed with truth should not initiate a disciple out of pride; one who does so would dwell in hell and become diseased in this life.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-napuṃsakāḥ striyaḥ śūdrā ye cānye@pi tadarthinaḥ / te dīkṣāyāṃ na mīmāṃsyā jñānakāle vicārayet jñānamūlo guruḥ proktaḥ saptasatrīṃ pravartayet / dīkṣā vyākhyā kṛpā maitrī śāstracintā śivaikatā annādidānamityetatpālayetsaptasatrakam / abhiṣekavidhau cāsmai karaṇīkhaṭikādikam sarvopakaraṇavrātamarpaṇīyaṃ vipaścite / so@bhiṣikto guruṃ paścāddakṣiṇābhiḥ prapūjayet jñānahīno guruḥ karmī svādhikāraṃ samarpya no / dīkṣādyadhikṛtiṃ kuryādvinā tasyājñayā punaḥ ityevaṃ śrāvayetso@pi namaskṛtyābhinandayet / tataḥ prabhṛtyasau pūrvo gurustyaktādhikārakaḥ yathecchaṃ vicaredvyākhyādīkṣādau yantraṇojjhitaḥ / kurvanna bādhyate yasmāddīpāddīpavadīdṛśaḥ santāno nādhikārasya cyavo@kurvanna bādhyate / prāk ca kurvanvihanyeta siddhātantre taducyate yathārthamupadeśaṃ tu kurvannācārya ucyate / na cāvajñā kriyākāle saṃsāroddharaṇaṃ prati na dīkṣeta guruḥ śiṣyaṃ tattvayuktastu garvataḥ / yo@sya syānnarake vāsa iha ca vyādhito bhavet

chunks.l2:
[tal-a23-v31] Having received consecration, that guru should for six months meditate upon and recite all the mantra-methods taught in the tantras, from oneness.

[tal-a23-v32] When one has truly become one with that, power is attained; then bonds are to be cut, and effort must be made to remain established in that identification.

[tal-a23-v33] A subtle line, like moon-crystal, rises from the heart cakra; it is sound-form, tranquil, and goes through the row of cakras.

[tal-a23-v34] Rooted at the twelfth end, that [form] lies in the suṣumnā between the three paths; there, having filled the heart cakra, one should mutter the blazing-bright mantra.

[tal-a23-v35] It resembles a thighlike flood of flame issuing through the holes of eyes and hair, scattered up to a quiet flame-tip, dissolving all ghee.

[tal-a23-v36] When the mind's inner space is satiated by a stream of ghee, mantras thus become givers of liberation; they would be radiant, awakened, and very pure.

[tal-a23-v37] It goes through the root, bulb, navel, heart, throat, and palate; through the half-moon, the end of sound, and the pervading power.

[tal-a23-v38] Where, in the circle of muttering, resting in the pure self and other circle, from all scattered distinction.

[tal-a23-v39] There, in the Tantra named after the Goddess, this vidyā-vow—called the great mantra—is declared for the accomplishment of mantra potency.

[tal-a23-v40] And that identity-only, as stated in the Spanda treatise, having overcome power, the mantras are of the all-knowing, power-possessing one.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-prāptābhiṣekaḥ sa guruḥ ṣaṇmāsānmantrapaddhatim / sarvāṃ tantroditāṃ dhyāyejjapeccātanmayatvataḥ yadaiva tanmayībhūtastadā vīryamupāgataḥ / chindyātpāśāṃstato yatnaṃ kuryāttanmayatāsthitau hṛccakrādutthitā sūkṣmā śaśisphaṭikasaṃnibhā / lekhākārā nādarūpā praśāntā cakrapaṅktigā dvādaśānte nirūḍhā sā sauṣumne tripathāntare / tatra hṛccakramāpūrya japenmantraṃ jvalatprabham cakṣurlomādirandhraughavahajjvālaurvasaṃnibham / yāvacchāntaśikhākīrṇaṃ viśvājyapravilāpakam tadājyadhārāsaṃtṛptamānābhikuharāntaram / evaṃ mantrā mokṣadāḥ syurdīptā buddhāḥ sunirmalāḥ mūlakandanabhonābhihṛtkaṇṭhālikatālugam / ardhendurodhikānādatadantavyāpiśaktigam samanonmanaśuddhātmaparacakrasamāśritam / yatra yatra japeccakre samastavyastabhedanāt tatra tatra mahāmantra iti devyākhyayāmale / vidyāvratamidaṃ proktaṃ mantravīryaprasiddhaye tacca tādātmyameveti yaduktaṃ spandaśāsane / tadākramya balaṃ mantrāḥ sarvajñabalaśālinaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a23-v41] Having completed the vow of knowledge, after initiation, explanation, and the like, in every way, they proceed for authority, like the instruments of embodied beings.

[tal-a23-v42] He should do this among fit disciples, never among unfit ones; in secret he should join a brahmin, having tested him contrariwise.

[tal-a23-v43] Power comes from conduct, not otherwise, according to the ūrmi teaching; the small daily practices should be performed as stated in the Brahmayāmala.

[tal-a23-v44] O dear, one who has completed the knowledge-vow remembers all by mind; but one whose all-knowing is concealed by bodily connection is a vessel of hypocrisy.

[tal-a23-v45] Even if he does not initiate, the teacher is never defiled; having recognized his unfitness, he would not initiate him, in order to avoid harm.

[tal-a23-v46] Having known him in knowledge, scripture, attainment, guru-ness, and so on, one should examine him again and again to see whether he possesses fitness for each [relevant qualification].

[tal-a23-v47] There one should appoint, never by reversal; for surely, whence arises desire for that unfit thing?

[tal-a23-v48] A desire empowered by that Lord indeed indicates his fitness; truly, some awakened desire does not attain establishment.

[tal-a23-v49] Just as a lightning-like sinful nature is abandoned, with rooted and unrooted states, so too that desire arises by Shambhu's grace.

[tal-a23-v50] Only one whose desire has not taken root is not a vessel for it; and one who, though possessing right knowledge, lacks faith in the guru.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-pravartante@dhikārāya karaṇānīva dehinām / kṛtavidyāvrataḥ paścāddīkṣāvyākhyādi sarvataḥ kuryādyogyeṣu śiṣyeṣu nāyogyeṣu kadācana / rahasye yojayedvipraṃ parīkṣya viparītataḥ ācārācchaktimapyeva nānyathetyūrmiśāsane / nityādyalpālpakaṃ kuryādyaduktaṃ brahmayāmale cīrṇavidyāvrataḥ sarvaṃ manasā vā smaretpriye / dehasaṃbandhasaṃchannasārvajñyo dambhabhājanam avidandīkṣamāṇo@pi na duṣyeddaiśikaḥ kvacit / jñātvā tvayogyatāṃ nainaṃ dīkṣeta pratyavāyitām buddhvā jñāne śāstrasiddhigurutvādau ca taṃ punaḥ / bhūya eva parīkṣeta tattadaucityaśālinam tatra tatra niyuñjīta natu jātu viparyayāt / nanu tadvastvayogyasya tatrecchā jāyate kutaḥ tadīśādhiṣṭhitecchaiva yogyatāmasya sūcayet / satyaṃ kāpi prabuddhāsāvicchā rūḍhiṃ na gacchati vidyudvatpāpaśīlasya yathā pāpāpavarjane / rūḍhyarūḍhī tadicchāyā api śaṃbhuprasādataḥ aprarūḍhatathecchākastata eva na bhājanam / yaḥ samyagjñānamādāya guruviśvāsavarjitaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a23-v51] If this is known here, the world would not be destroyed; knowledge should be bestowed; even if it is unknown, when it is known again, one should practice the removal of knowledge.

[tal-a23-v52] When it is known again and again yet lacks trust, then one should meditate before him, throbbing like the moon and sun.

[tal-a23-v53] Then one should meditate on the deluding left power, which rises from the sky of wisdom of one's own heart-lotus and is darkened by Rahu.

[tal-a23-v54] Having contemplated her as having emerged by the left-hand procedure and as proceeding toward the goal, one should contemplate him as light swallowed by her.

[tal-a23-v55] By this sequence-yoga, for one of deluded mind and evil soul, knowledge, mantra, science, and the like cause harm.

[tal-a23-v56] But how could knowledge situated in the self be taken away? Therefore how is knowledge-removal said to be preceded by śrī?

[tal-a23-v57] It is said: since the disciple's knowledge has fully matured, why should it be removed from one who possesses complete fitness?

[tal-a23-v58] But this fool is deeply made by the Lord's Vāmā power by nature alone; therefore his vidyā and the rest are harmful.

[tal-a23-v59] Again, the teacher is identical with Shiva; if the consecrated one performs the fivefold action, then his full authority is that.

[tal-a23-v60] So the guru is authorized over the fourfold task — creation and maintenance of the pure realities, their impurity and their dissolution — through the joining (of the paths) and grace.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-lokaṃ viplāvayennāsmiñjñāte vijñānamarpayet / ajñāte@pi punarjñāte vijñānaharaṇaṃ caret punaḥpunaryadā jñāto viśvāsaparivarjitaḥ / tadā tamagrato dhyāyetsphurantaṃ candrasūryavat tato nijahṛdambhojabodhāmbarataloditām / svarbhānumalināṃ dhyāyedvāmāṃ śaktiṃ vimohanīm vāmācārakrameṇaināṃ niḥsṛtāṃ sādhyagāminīm / cintayitvā tayā grastaprakāśaṃ taṃ vicintayet anena kramayogena mūḍhabuddherdurātmanaḥ / vijñānamantravidyādyāḥ prakurvantyapakāritām nanu vijñānamātmasthaṃ kathaṃ hartuṃ kṣamaṃ bhavet / ato vijñānaharaṇaṃ kathaṃ śrīpūrva ucyate ucyate nāsya śiṣyasya vijñānaṃ rūḍhimāgatam / tathātve haraṇaṃ kasmātpūrṇayogyatvaśālinaḥ kiṃtveṣa vāmayā śaktyā mūḍho gāḍhaṃ vibhoḥ kṛtaḥ / svabhāvādeva tenāsya vidyādyamapakārakam guruḥ punaḥ śivābhinnaḥ sanyaḥ pañcavidhāṃ kṛtim / kuryādyadi tataḥ pūrṇamadhikāritvamasya tat ato yathā śuddhatattvasṛṣṭisthityormalātyaye / yojanānugrahe kāryacatuṣke@dhikṛto guruḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a23-v61] By non-difference from Shiva, he performs that; like the fifth, this too is the duty called disappearance; thus that one is of Shiva-nature.

[tal-a23-v62] Therefore, indeed, in Shiva, in scripture, in knowledge, and in the vessel of reassurance, even the abode of anger is not hidden by the guru's foolishness.

[tal-a23-v63] Indeed, one whose teacher is angered is called hidden, a worldly being; yet he is God indeed—not a teacher, nor a false knower.

[tal-a23-v64] Therefore, although the defamer of scriptures and the like is not burned by the angry guru, yet he is obscured.

[tal-a23-v65] This is the coming of our teacher: when he is hidden in a child, one should not be angry, nor should the wise one curse, for he is indeed always a benefactor.

[tal-a23-v66] If, impelled by the Lord's will, he strangles the bond in his throat, what is the teacher to do for him there? Would there be cooperation?

[tal-a23-v67] Even though the guru is non-different from Shiva, he is indeed the Lord's principal, grace-filled power; one devoted to that power should be graced by him in every way.

[tal-a23-v68] But scripture is spoken only to awaken awareness of freedom; it is not an action to perform. For those who are falling, a hand-support is acceptable, but making them fall is not.

[tal-a23-v69] Therefore, having purified him with expiations, the guru should initiate him with compassion, since he is again facing the desire for independence and the like.

[tal-a23-v70] Approaching with an upward gaze and then being well reassured, one approaches the supreme; even by approaching the lower scripture, one may not attain worthiness of good.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-śivābhedena tatkuryāttadvatpañcamamapyayam / tirobhāvābhidhaṃ kṛtyaṃ tathāsau śivatātmakaḥ ata eva śive śāstre jñāne cāśvāsabhājanam / gurormūḍhatayā kopadhāmāpi na tirohitaḥ gururhi kupito yasya sa tirohita ucyate / saṃsārī satu devo hi gururna ca mṛṣāvidaḥ tata eva ca śāstrādidūṣako yadyapi krudhā / na dahyate@sau guruṇā tathāpyeṣa tirohitaḥ asmadgurvāgamastveṣa tirobhūte svayaṃ śiśau / na kupyenna śapeddhīmān sa hyanugrāhakaḥ sadā īśecchācoditaḥ pāśaṃ yadi kaṇṭhe nipīḍayet / kimācāryeṇa tatrāsya kāryā syātsahakāritā śivābhinno@pi hi gururanugrahamayīṃ vibhoḥ / mukhyāṃ śaktimupāsīno@nugṛhṇīyātsa sarvathā svātantryamātrajñaptyai tu kathitaṃ śāstra īdṛśam / na kāryaṃ patatāṃ hastālambaḥ sahyo na pātanam ata eva svatantratvādicchāyāḥ punarunmukham / prāyaścittairviśodhyainaṃ dīkṣeta kṛpayā guruḥ ūrdhvadṛṣṭau prapannaḥ sannanāśvastastataḥ param / adhaḥśāstraṃ prapadyāpi na śreyaḥpātratāmiyāt

chunks.l2:
[tal-a23-v71] One fallen into downward vision, whose mind is not reassured by it, yet holding the upward command: sin; let him abandon that and become Shiva.

[tal-a23-v72] Even a minister, though a limb of the king, is ruined if he harms the king; but the reversal is not the same—one should resort to the upward view.

[tal-a23-v73] In the earlier Śrī-śāstra it was stated by him: as long as it is not extracted by him alone, here the meaning is this much, augmented by prior knowledge.

[tal-a23-v74] Thus here the guru is indeed the one referred to by that word: one who possesses such practiced knowledge and holds high status.

[tal-a23-v75] One who has not been uplifted has no welfare; welfare arises through upliftment by the guru, whether this one or another. Therefore the example of the lotus-born and the sun is explained here.

[tal-a23-v76] The light of the three worlds is one; indeed another light is night-made; knowledge is another for the Trika guru, and another for those dwelling in your nature.

[tal-a23-v77] Therefore, when one is in the state of a former guru, then one should again resort to that other who is endowed with marks, facing upward.

[tal-a23-v78] If that state is present, the upward-facing one should not abandon it out of doubt; clearly, doing so would be a fault—one of two possible courses—that destroys authority.

[tal-a23-v79] Here the fault is not determined as a fault simply because it stands in the world; rather, that one is considered to be of a nature connected with explaining ignorance.

[tal-a23-v80] Even for the disciple, the chief fault is the unsteady form of such knowledge; other faults arise from it.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-adhodṛṣṭau prapannastu tadanāśvastamānasaḥ / ūrdhvaśāsanabhāk pāpaṃ taccojjhecca śivībhavet rājñe druhyannamātyāṅgabhūto@pi hi vihanyate / viparyayastu netyevamūrdhvāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ samāśrayet śrīpūrvaśāstre tenoktaṃ yāvattenaiva noddhṛtaḥ / atra hyartho@yametāvatpūrvoktajñānavṛṃhitaḥ gurustāvatsa evātra tacchabdenāvamṛśyate / tādṛksvabhyastavijñānabhājordhvapadaśālinā anuddhṛtasya na śreya etadanyagurūddhṛteḥ / ata evāmbujanmārkadṛṣṭānto@tra nirūpitaḥ trijagajjyotiṣo hyanyattejo@nyacca niśākṛtaḥ / jñānamanyattrikaguroranyattvadharavartinām ata eva purābhūtagurvabhāvo yadā tadā / tadanyaṃ lakṣaṇopetamāśrayetpunarunmukhaḥ sati tasmiṃstūnmukhaḥ sankasmājjahyādyadi sphuṭam / syādanyatarago doṣo yo@dhikārāpaghātakaḥ doṣaśceha na lokastho doṣatvena nirūpyate / ajñānakhyāpanāyuktakhyāpanātmā tvasau mataḥ śiṣyasyāpi tathābhūtajñānānāśvastarūpatā / mukhyo doṣastadanye hi doṣāstatprabhavā yataḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a23-v81] Who indeed greatly esteems a physician when disease is already destroyed? Surely an envious one, whose disease is destroyed, becomes healthy by force.

[tal-a23-v82] Thus, one comforted by knowledge—what should he not do for the guru? If not indeed untrusted, he stands like one trusted.

[tal-a23-v83] In the Mālinīvijayottara it is said that the faults beginning with ignorance belonging to the guru are not worldly faults, in order to declare this.

[tal-a23-v84] One should not investigate his conduct, whether auspicious or inauspicious; he himself knows whether it is proper or improper.

[tal-a23-v85] When someone is attached to forbidden things that steal life and wealth, that person should be restrained by a humble wise one.

[tal-a23-v86] A forbidden act is defined by its stated intention; even if someone is strongly restrained by another, if he does not turn back, the matter remains unresolved in the supplied fragment.

[tal-a23-v87] Then, having gone elsewhere, one should meditate on Śiva alone; indeed there is no fault in his guru-hood by which one would farm a barren field.

[tal-a23-v88] At night one should act or go; or he, a thief of wealth and life, fearing his displeasure, should then behave in that way.

[tal-a23-v89] Because it is unpleasant, he will not hear what is spoken; in Śrīmātaṅga it is said, and it is not studied out of fear of the earth.

[tal-a23-v90] What is said as 'this much is to be done' is firm; for those seized by intense power, it shines by itself in the heart.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-na dhvastavyādhikaḥ ko hi bhiṣajaṃ bahu manyate / asūyurnūnamadhvastavyādhiḥ svasthāyate balāt evaṃ jñānasamāśvastaḥ kiṃ kiṃ na gurave caret / no cennūnamaviśvasto viśvasta iva tiṣṭhati ajñānādaya evaite doṣā na laukikā guroḥ / iti khyāpayituṃ proktaṃ mālinīvijayottare na tasyānveṣayedvṛttaṃ śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham / sa eva tadvijānāti yuktaṃ cāyuktameva vā akāryeṣu yadā saktaḥ prāṇadravyāpahāriṣu / tadā nivāraṇīyo@sau praṇatena vipaścitā viśeṣaṇamakāryāṇāmuktābhiprāyameva yat / tenātivāryamāṇo@pi yadyasau na nivartate tadānyatra kvacidgatvā śivamevānucintayet / na hyasya sa gurutve syāddoṣo yenoṣare kṛṣim kuryādvrajenniśāyāṃ vā sa tvarthaprāṇahārakaḥ / tadīyāpriyabhīrustu paraṃ tādṛśamācaret yatastadapriyaṃ naiṣa śṛṇuyāditi bhāṣitam / śrīmātaṅge taduktaṃ ca nādhītaṃ bhūmabhītitaḥ yaccaitaduktametāvatkartavyamiti taddhruvam / tīvraśaktigṛhītānāṃ svayameva hṛdi sphuret

chunks.l2:
[tal-a23-v100] This is called the path of teachers for whom karma predominates: the station or world of the six-half-teacher and ardhanari.

[tal-a23-v91] This teaching is declared to gradually kindle one's own power for those of weak or medium capacity; that power then blazes sufficiently.

[tal-a23-v92] Those who partake in the abundance of beautiful ardor born of firm attachment are self-exultant; love is all; firmness elsewhere is seen.

[tal-a23-v93] Indeed, why is this an example? What inauspicious thing has been done by it? Consciousness-pulsation is all-pervading; from a different substrate, he is thus, thus.

[tal-a23-v94] Even one who is hidden and again becomes manifest is liberated by himself, even without a teacher.

[tal-a23-v95] This manner is not stated here; it arises from the strength of śaktipāta; and here, by impossibility, it is like firm anger and favor.

[tal-a23-v96] Thus this rule declared by the teacher: the teacher should protect it; otherwise he would not attain auspiciousness in the glorious essence, as described.

[tal-a23-v97] Those teachers who wrongly carry out the scriptural meaning and sufficiently abandon it, dwelling in Ardhanārīśapura, are fallen from the vow.

[tal-a23-v98] Elsewhere too there is authority, which would lead to lordship of vidyā; elsewhere, by abandoning the vow, one becomes a flesh-eater for a hundred years.

[tal-a23-v99] Such is the meaning there; the Siddhanta guru's conclusion is that one becomes lord of piśāca-vidyā, but the tantric is indeed pure.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-upadeśastvayaṃ mandamadhyaśakternijāṃ kramāt / śaktiṃ jvalayituṃ proktaḥ sā hyevaṃ jājvalītyalam dṛḍhānurāgasubhagasaṃrambhābhogabhāginaḥ / svollāsi smarasarvasyaṃ dārḍhyāyānyatra dṛśyate nanveṣa kasmāddṛṣṭāntaḥ kimetenāśubhaṃ kṛtam / citspandaḥ sarvago bhinnādupādheḥ sa tathā tathā bhavetko@pi tirobhūtaḥ punarunmukhito@pi san / vināpi daiśikātprāgvatsvayameva vimucyate prakārastveṣa nātroktaḥ śaktipātabalādgataḥ / asaṃbhāvyatayā cātra dṛḍhakopaprasādavat ityeṣa yo guroḥ prokto vidhistaṃ pālayedguruḥ / anyathā na śivaṃ yāyācchrīmatsāre ca varṇitam anyāyaṃ ye prakurvanti śāstrārthaṃ varjayantyalam / te@rdhanārīśapuragā guravaḥ samayacyutāḥ anyatrāpyadhikāraṃ ca neyādvidyeśatāṃ vrajet / anyatra samayatyāgātkravyādatvaṃ śataṃ samāḥ iyattatratyatātparyaṃ siddhāntagururunnayaḥ / bhavetpiśācavidyeśaḥ śuddha eva tu tāntrikaḥ ṣaḍardhadaiśikaścārdhanārīśabhuvanasthitiḥ / eṣā karmapradhānānāṃ gurūṇāṃ gatirucyate

chunks.l2:
[tal-a23-v101] For knowers, this is not bondage; thus it is stated everywhere. Even in the adept's consecration, all this rite is said.

[tal-a23-v102] Here there is no conferral of authority and no knowledge-vow; rather, an accomplishable mantra is conferred within one's own useful sequence of rites.

[tal-a23-v103] In the complete teaching, one should offer one's own implements; the consecration rite is determined by the Supreme Lord, as it has been determined.
